title: Rialto Theatre pit band with Emil Williams
summary: He moved to the Rialto pit band with Emil Williams on piano and violinist Guy Taylor; Smith explains he wants the career in sequence first.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: That's what we used to do. And let's see, after I left there -- I came to the Rialto, I think.
Yeah, Rialto Theatre, yeah, 18th and Hyland.
What was that in the pit band there, or were you all part of the stage?
Yeah, pit band, yeah. Emil Williams playing piano.
Anybody else in that band we should know about?
Well, I didn't -- let's see. Goobie, his real name was Guy Taylor. He was a violinist.

Well, I'm going to get to the personalities later on, Baby, but I thought, you know, when you mentioned Basie at the Eblon Theatre, and him playing a blues when he's supposed to be playing that sneaky type music for a

silent thing, I thought it belonged in there. But we're going to get to all the people later on, but I'm interested, you know, I think we're all interested in the sort of sequence of events right up to today because I know what was happening just recently. You and I were playing around the corner from each- other when you were at Huck Finns and we were at Vitale's Batelly's Vil- lage Gate.

But inbetween now from the Rialto where did you go? And if you can sort of the years, you know, early thirties, '32, '33. You see, we skipped -- you were born in 1894 and we're already up to the early thirties. Charles, did you have something you wanted to say?
